MLC LLM is a general compiler and inference engine that deploys language models on GPUs, in browsers through WebGPU, and on iOS and Android behind an OpenAI-compatible API. It has no GUI, browser or device interaction of its own, so it falls outside the computer-use scope.

ms-swift is ModelScope's general framework for fine-tuning, aligning and deploying several hundred language and multimodal models with methods such as SFT, DPO and GRPO. Its README describes no GUI, browser or device interaction; GUI-agent projects mention it only as their training toolkit.

github.com/modelscope/swift is the former name of modelscope/ms-swift: the GitHub API returns the same repository ID, 673412924, for both names. PaLM-E is an embodied multimodal language model that feeds images and robot state estimates into PaLM for robotic manipulation planning, visual question answering and captioning. Its project page describes no interaction with graphical interfaces, web pages or devices, so it falls outside the computer-use scope.

The Claude Agent SDK packages the Claude Code agent loop as a Python and TypeScript library whose built-in tools read and edit files, run shell commands and search the web. The overview lists no graphical, browser or device-control executor, so it is a general agent framework outside the computer-use scope.

Collaborative Gym (Co-Gym) is a framework for human-agent collaboration whose agents act through API-style tools (travel search functions, a distance matrix, paper search and library actions, Jupyter cells and a shared text editor) in travel planning, related-work writing and tabular analysis tasks. Its agents do not operate graphical, browser or device interfaces, so the paper is outside the catalog's computer-use and GUI-agent scope.

Relevance AI is a no-code platform for building sales, marketing, support and operations agents that act through 1,000+ app integrations, evals and governance controls. Its only page interaction comes from optional tool steps for Airtop, a separate browser service that needs its own account, so it is a general agent-builder platform rather than a computer-use resource.

A 22 October 2024 post on Simon Willison's personal weblog recounting his first runs of Anthropic's computer-use-demo Docker container and commenting on coordinate output, prompt injection risk and model naming. It is commentary on the already-curated Claude computer-use capability (url:57f17b7d0c18b2d7c8bf), not a new agent, dataset, benchmark or tool.

rl4vlm.github.io is the project page of arXiv 2405.10292, which fine-tunes a LLaVA vision-language model with PPO and chain-of-thought prompts on GymCards arithmetic card games and the ALFWorld embodied household environment. Neither task operates a web page, desktop or mobile interface, so the work is outside the computer-use scope.

robotics-transformer2.github.io presents RT-2, a vision-language-action model that co-fine-tunes web-scale vision-language models on robot trajectories so they output physical robot actions for manipulation tasks. It controls a robot arm, not web, desktop or mobile interfaces, so it is outside the computer-use scope.

scrapegraphai.com is the hosted API for ScrapeGraphAI, which turns web pages into Markdown, screenshots or prompt-defined JSON and offers search, site crawling and change-monitoring endpoints plus an MCP server. It retrieves and extracts page content for LLM pipelines and does not let an agent operate a web interface, so it is a crawler outside the computer-use scope.

SerpApi is a commercial API that returns search-engine result pages from Google, Bing, Baidu, DuckDuckGo and shopping or app-store sites as parsed JSON. Callers send queries over HTTP and never open or operate a web page, so it is search-data infrastructure rather than computer or browser use.

Serper is a commercial API that returns Google search results (web, images, news, maps, places, shopping, scholar and patents) as JSON for programmatic use. It does not open or operate web pages or other interfaces, so it is search-data infrastructure rather than computer or browser use.

Superhighway is a hosted web search API for AI agents whose endpoints return ranked results, news, image links and page text as markdown, sold per call with a free tier. It never renders, clicks or types in a page or app, so it is retrieval infrastructure rather than a computer-use agent, environment or tool.

A 3 March 2025 TechCrunch news item by Ivan Mehta reporting Opera's announcement of Browser Operator, a preview agent that completes tasks on websites inside the user's own browser, based on Opera's demo video and claims. It is third-party press coverage, not an agent, dataset, benchmark or tool.

A 4 November 2025 Anthropic engineering post arguing that agents should call Model Context Protocol tools by writing code in an execution environment, which cuts the tokens spent on tool definitions and intermediate results. It concerns API tool integration and never involves operating graphical interfaces, websites or devices.

A February 2026 Anthropic research post that measures how much autonomy people grant agents, using privacy-preserving analysis of Claude Code sessions and tool calls on the public API: turn durations, auto-approval and interruption rates, and the risk of tool actions. It studies coding and API tool use, not agents operating graphical interfaces, websites or devices.

Expand is a commercial API that renders web pages in a hosted browser and returns them as Markdown together with the page's embedded JSON and a citable snapshot, with crawl and change-monitoring endpoints. Agents receive page content but never click, type or otherwise operate a page, so it is retrieval infrastructure rather than computer or browser use.

An October 2024 Interconnects newsletter post by Nathan Lambert that gives first impressions of Anthropic's Computer Use beta from two trial web tasks and then compares the Anthropic, Google and OpenAI frontier models. It is third-party commentary with no dataset, code, model or evaluation of its own, so it is not a catalog resource.

A 9 November 2023 Gates Notes essay in which Bill Gates predicts that personal AI agents, acting across applications from everyday-language requests, will reshape health care, education, productivity and shopping within five years, and lists open questions about privacy and agent-to-agent protocols. It is opinion commentary with no system, method, data or evaluation and does not discuss operating graphical interfaces.

A 2017 Kaggle upload by user Mitchell J of 13,000 images scraped by sequential URL from the prnt.sc screenshot-sharing site, with a hand-labelled subset in six content categories (animations, games, objects, people, text, one game character). The images are arbitrary user uploads with no interface annotations, actions or tasks, and the license is given only as 'Data files (c) Original Authors', so it is not a GUI-agent resource.

UISketch is a CHI 2021 dataset of about 19,000 hand-drawn sketches of 21 UI element categories from 1,218 participants, released on Kaggle with image-classification checkpoints for sketch-based UI prototyping. It contains no screenshots, interface states or interactions, so it supports design tooling rather than agents that perceive or operate interfaces.

This Future Internet 2025 article proposes a framework that combines model-driven development with generative AI and multi-agent reinforcement learning to personalize and re-lay-out e-commerce user interfaces from collected user behavior data. Its agents generate and optimize interface designs for human users; no agent perceives or operates a graphical interface, so it is outside the catalog's scope.

This Microsoft Research page lists the February 2024 arXiv paper 2402.05929, which trains one multi-task agent foundation model with masked visual autoencoding, language modeling and next-action prediction and evaluates it on robotics, gaming and healthcare video tasks. It does not study agents that operate web, desktop or mobile interfaces, so it is outside the catalog's scope.

This Nature Communications article (2026; arXiv 2508.04039) shows that large reasoning models can autonomously run persuasive multi-turn text conversations that jailbreak other chat models. The attacks happen only in conversation, with no browser, GUI, tool or device actions, so it concerns language-model safety rather than computer-use agents.

Context.dev is a commercial web data API whose endpoints scrape a URL into Markdown, JSON or screenshots, search the web, crawl sites in batches, answer questions with sources and watch pages for changes. Its optional pre-capture browser actions only click, scroll or wait to load content, so it is retrieval infrastructure rather than an agent, environment or tool for operating interfaces.

Ethan Mollick's One Useful Thing post of 22 October 2024 gives first impressions of Anthropic's Claude computer use, from a lesson-planning task and a run at the Paperclip Clicker browser game, with prompting hints from Anthropic. It is third-party commentary that releases no software, data or evaluation of its own.

A DataCamp blog tutorial by Abid Ali Awan, dated 22 October 2024, that explains Anthropic's computer-use beta, shows its tool definitions, walks through running Anthropic's reference Docker demo and lists prompting tips, limitations and token pricing. It is third-party instructional content about a resource rather than a resource of its own.

SocialCrawl is a commercial data API that returns public profiles, posts, comments and search results from social and commerce platforms in one JSON schema, with an MCP server and SDKs for agents. It retrieves data through API calls and does not operate browser, desktop or mobile interfaces, so it is data-retrieval infrastructure rather than a computer-use resource.

CLONE is a USENIX ATC 2025 systems paper on serving large language models on edge devices through model- and system-level co-design with a 28nm hardware accelerator, measured on latency and energy. It does not build, train or evaluate agents that operate graphical, web or mobile interfaces, so it is general on-device LLM inference rather than a computer-use resource.

swebench.com hosts the official leaderboards of the SWE-bench family (the original 2,294-instance set, Verified, Bash Only, Lite, Multilingual and Multimodal) and links its tooling. These benchmarks score models on resolving GitHub issues by editing repository code and passing tests, without operating a graphical, browser or device interface, so the site falls outside the computer-use scope; only the Multimodal subset, reviewed separately, involves visual inputs.

This page is the project website of Symbol-LLM (arXiv 2311.09278), which instruction-tunes language models on 34 symbolic tasks such as SQL, knowledge-graph queries, code, logic and planning. It does not build or evaluate agents that operate graphical, web or mobile interfaces, so the page and the paper are outside the computer-use scope.
